chunks: "Whatever you use to converse privately with your Lord during the salat (prayer) is not considered speech."

key_terms.رَبَّكَ: your Lord, the One being addressed in worship
key_terms.نَاجَيْتَ: you privately conversed or intimately addressed

ai.seo_question: Does speaking to Allah during salat count as ordinary speech that invalidates the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith states that words by which a worshipper privately addresses Allah within the salat (prayer) are not treated as ordinary human speech. It indicates a fiqh distinction between devotional address to Allah and invalidating speech during prayer.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.939 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:
"Whatever you use to converse with your Lord (azj) during prayer is not considered ordinary speech”.
